---
title: "Film & TV"
subtitle: "Screen appearances and later cultural visibility"
---

```{python}
import duckdb
from IPython.display import display

con = duckdb.connect("../data/processed/music_life.duckdb", read_only=True)

usage = con.execute("""
SELECT recording_title, appearances, movies, tv_episodes,
       earliest_screen_date, latest_screen_date
FROM screen_usage_summary
WHERE appearances > 0
ORDER BY appearances DESC, recording_title
""").df()

display(usage)
```

## What this layer measures

The chart layer describes **contemporary popularity**. Film and television use
can provide a different signal: **later cultural visibility**.

For each focus artist/album the production dashboard can show:

- movies containing a work/recording;
- exact TV episodes where available;
- earliest and most recent documented screen use;
- use type such as background, performance or credits when sourced;
- total screen appearances by track;
- Spotify links back to confidently matched recordings.

## Evidence model

A film/TV title and a soundtrack observation are separate facts.

TMDB is used primarily for canonical movie/series/episode metadata and external
identifiers. The actual assertion that a song or recording appeared on screen
must come from a source that supports that assertion.

When the source identifies the song but not the exact recording, the database
should link the **work** rather than guessing a recording.

## Future analysis

Screen appearances can eventually be compared with historical chart success,
covers, samples and streaming availability to explore cultural longevity. Any
combined "longevity" measure is a project-derived metric and must be labelled
accordingly.
